metric_methodology.correctness: Expected-fact coverage using normalized lexical overlap. A fact is supported when answer/fact token overlap is >= 0.60. This is a heuristic proxy and not a substitute for human semantic review.
metric_methodology.response_relevance: Question-answer token overlap: >=0.50 = full relevance, >=0.25 = partial relevance, otherwise zero.
metric_methodology.retrieval_evidence_hit_rate: Number of retrieved chunks containing lexical support for at least one expected fact divided by retrieved chunks.
metric_methodology.retrieval_gold_coverage: Retrieved gold source/page locations divided by the number of gold source/page locations specified in the rubric, capped at 100%.
metric_methodology.hallucination_signal_rate: Rate of answers triggering conservative unsupported-claim patterns. This is a screening signal, not a confirmed hallucination rate.
metric_methodology.composite_test_pass_rate: Successful generation plus correctness >=60%, relevance >=50%, and at least one retrieval chunk with evidence support. Q25 requires abstention.
metric_methodology.latency: Wall-clock generation latency recorded by the evaluation runner.
metric_methodology.token_usage: Prompt, output, and total tokens returned by Ollama.
metric_methodology.resource_usage: Evaluator-process CPU percentage snapshots and memory delta. These are not isolated Ollama model resource measurements.
metric_methodology.ai_output_testing: Independent pass/fail checks covering relevance, retrieved-context support, unsupported-claim screening, expected format, answering when information exists, and abstention when information is unavailable.

questions.question: What biometric information is collected for Aadhaar?
questions.answer:
Biometrics, also known as fingerprints and facial recognition data (FRD), are a type of unique identification method that uses physical characteristics such as the shape or size of an object to verify someone's identity. 

In Aadhaar system, biometric information is collected for verification purposes:
1. Fingerprint Data - This includes finger print patterns and sizes used by users in daily life activities like walking, sitting, standing etc., which are unique identifiers that can be scanned or captured using a device with an infrared sensor (like smartphones). 
2. Face Recognition data- Aadhaar uses facial recognition technology to verify the identity of individuals who use their mobile phones and computers for daily life activities like walking, sitting etc., by comparing face images in real time from users' devices or cameras using algorithms that are trained on a large database containing pictures of people with known identities.
3. Voice Recognition data - Aadhaar also uses voice recognition technology to verify the identity and authenticity of individuals who use their mobile phones for daily life activities, by comparing spoken language patterns in real time from users' devices or microphones using algorithms that are trained on a large database containing recordings (sounds) of people with known identities.
4. Hardware Tokens - These tokens generated during the enrollment process can be used to verify Aadhaar ID, which includes fingerprint data and face/voice recognition information from users' devices or smartphones in future transactions for secure authentication purposes. 
5. Biometric Verification Data- This is a unique identifier that uniquely identifies an individual using biometrics (finger print patterns) to verify their identity at the point of registration, during online services and on mobile applications like UID AI etc., which are used by government authorities for verification in Aadhaar systems.

questions.question: What documents can be used as proof of identity?
questions.answer:
The list provided in UIAI_2.pdf page number three (Criteria for acceptability of the documents submitted to evidence Identity, Address and Date Of Birth) does not contain specific criteria that all Aadhaar Proofs should meet before they can be used as proof of identity or address/date-of-birth information in a user's context. 

However, it is generally accepted among the users (and legal entities), for any document to serve as evidence Identity and Address will need at least:
1) To contain an image with name along side date & time of creation or last update; this can be done using Aadhaar card itself. 
2) The information should not have been tampered in the process, ie., it must remain unchanged after being created/updated on a physical device (like smartphone). This is to ensure that even if someone else accesses your data from another source or location they cannot alter this document for themselves without changing its content.
3) The name of person should be mentioned along with the image in such documents, so as not only can it serve identity but also serves a purpose (like proofing an event). 
4) It must contain at least one date-of-birth and/or birth certificate if applicable for children under five years. This is to ensure that even though they are younger than sixteen the document will be valid, as per Aadhaar's rules of dating from a child (five or more).
5) The documents should not contain any other information apart from these four mentioned above which can serve identity and address/date-of-birth. 
6) It must have been submitted in the name that is being enrolled, otherwise it cannot be used as proof of Identity for a person under sixteen years old or older because Aadhaar rules do not allow this (unless they are children). This can also serve to prove their identity if someone else accesses your data from another source.

questions.question: Can a resident update Aadhaar information?
questions.answer:

Please note that the process may vary based on various factors like location of residence (Aadhaar enrolment centre), language preference, and other specific requirements set by UIDAI or your local government for updating personal details such as DOB in Aadhaars due to privacy concerns related with these sensitive attributes.

questions.question: What types of information can be updated in Aadhaar?
questions.answer:
In an Aadhaar (Individual Universal ID), the following details are typically updatable by users. These include name, address, date of birth and gender if they wish to change them due to any reason such as marriage or divorce etc., along with biometric data like photographs, fingerprints, iris scans for identification verification purposes:

1. Name - This is the full legal first name + last name (if applicable). The Aadhaar system will update this information in real-time and it'll be visible to all users who have access to your account on any mobile or web application, including those using a different device for accessing same data if you choose.
2. Address - This is the complete address where one lives with full details (street name + house number). The Aadhaar system will update this information in real-time and it'll be visible to all users who have access to your account on any mobile or web application, including those using a different device for accessing same data if you choose.
3. Date of Birth - This is the date when one was born (in DDMMYY format). The Aadhaar system will update this information in real-time and it'll be visible to all users who have access to your account on any mobile or web application, including those using a different device for accessing same data if you choose.
4. Gender - This is the gender of one (Male/Female). The Aadhaar system will update this information in real-time and it'll be visible to all users who have access to your account on any mobile or web application, including those using a different device for accessing same data if you choose.
5. Mobile Number - This is the phone number where one lives with full details (country code + actual Phone No). The Aadhaar system will update this information in real-time and it'll be visible to all users who have access to your account on any mobile or web application, including those using a different device for accessing same data if you choose.
6. Email ID - This is the email address where one lives with full details (email id + domain). The Aadhaar system will update this information in real-time and it'll be visible to all users who have access to your account on any mobile or web application, including those using a different device for accessing same data if you choose.
7. Biometric Data - This includes photographs (if one has taken them), fingerprints/iris scans(for identification verification purposes). The Aadhaar system will update these details in real-time and it'll be visible to all users who have access to your account on any mobile or web application, including those using a different device for accessing same data if you choose.
